key: And I will give peace in the land, and ye shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid; and I will cause evil beasts to cease out of the land, neither shall the sword go through your land.
s: Among the blessings for keeping the statutes comes safety in the land; Ramban, on 26:6, takes the ‘evil beasts’ as ceasing to harm, the land, while the commandments are kept, being as the world was before Adam’s sin, when no beast killed a man.

evidence.words: ועל דעת רבי שמעון שאמר משביתן שלא יזיקו (שם) יאמר והשבתי רעת החיות מן הארץ והוא הנכון כי תהיה ארץ ישראל בעת קיום המצות כאשר היה העולם מתחילתו קודם חטאו של אדם הראשון אין חיה ורמש ממית אדם
evidence.gloss: And according to Rabbi Shimon, who said that He makes them cease from doing harm, it means: I will make the evil of the beasts cease out of the land; and this is the correct view, for the land of Israel, at the time the commandments are kept, will be as the world was at its beginning, before the sin of the first man, when no beast or creeping thing killed a man.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Leviticus 26:6, at [115,6] match). Plain sense faithful: 26:3 to 13 are the blessings promised if the statutes are kept, and 26:6 is the promise of peace and safety in the land. Ramban on 26:6, והשבתי חיה רעה מן הארץ, sets out Rabbi Yehudah (beasts removed) and Rabbi Shimon (beasts made harmless), calls the second the correct one, and explains that the land of Israel, while the commandments are kept, will be as the world was before the first man’s sin, when no beast or creeping thing killed a man. The sentence carries exactly that. Rashi (peace outweighs all; the sword not even passing through), Ibn Ezra (peace among yourselves) and Leviticus Rabbah 35 were read and do not conflict. entry-check ok.
